title: AI-Related US Stocks: Three Market Phases
repairTitle: An 86% rebound, but very different recoveries
repairIntro: Set the initial price to 100 to see how much of the first loss was recovered. A low base after a large decline magnifies percentage gains.
repairTakeaway: TEM and SNDK both rebounded about 86%: TEM recovered about 218% of its first loss, versus only 69% for SNDK. LITE and DELL also exceeded their starting prices; MU did not fully recover, and KXIAY recovered only about 45%.
repairCaution: Recovery at the endpoint does not imply low risk: the largest closing drawdowns during phase 3 were 25.0% for TEM and 33.6% for LITE, versus 11.8% for NVDA. The endpoint is an October 30 intraday quote; KXIAY is delayed by at least 15 minutes.
speedTitle: A fast rally is only part of the story
speedIntro: All returns start at the July 29 close. The first 10 trading days end on August 12; the full rebound ends on September 22.
speedNote: CRWV rose 77.1% in the first 10 days but finished the rebound up only 42.7%; AAOI fell back from 80.4% to 39.8%. CRM gained just 2.6% in the first 10 days and 24.1% over the full window, with most of its gain arriving later.

lenses.label: Who outperformed NVDA in all three phases?
lenses.body: Each of these four securities had a higher endpoint return than NVDA in all three phases. They are listed in order of increasing historical volatility. MSFT's volatility was close to NVDA's; the other three were more volatile. Historical strength and low risk are different conclusions.

lenses.label: Who recovered more of the initial loss?
lenses.body: All four recovered their first-phase losses. TEM rebounded about 85.8% and lost less than NVDA in phase 3. AMD and DELL rebounded more than NVDA, but then fell about 20.6% and 24.2%, respectively, so their advantage was not consistent across phases.

lenses.label: Who rallied quickly, then gave more back?
lenses.body: CRWV and AAOI gained more in the first 10 days than over the full rebound. IREN fell about 52.1% in phase 3. KXIAY's large rebound recovered only about 45% of its initial loss. Deep declines and high sensitivity alone do not establish higher returns in the next cycle.

lenses.label: Does resilience also mean a stronger rebound?
lenses.body: Both had lower historical volatility and gained about 7.5% and 1.8% in phase 3. Yet they lost about 7.2% and 2.8% in the common rebound window. Reducing volatility and seeking a larger rebound are different allocation objectives.

sensitivityTitle: Can two days change the conclusion?
sensitivityIntro: Move the rebound start from July 29 to July 31, keeping September 22 as the endpoint. Including or excluding earnings-related jumps can change the ranking.
sensitivityNote: MSFT changes from +27.8% to +7.4%; CRM from +24.1% to +27.0%. PLTR is around +50% under either definition. Shifting the start by two days does not eliminate the effects of earnings jumps.
eventNote: Events shape the path: CRM rose about 22.6% on August 27 and PLTR about 29.5% on August 4. At the snapshot date, TEM was scheduled to report before the open on November 2 and PLTR after the close that day. Strong historical performance does not remove event risk.

introLead: A drawdown, a rebound, and another drawdown. Compare 78 AI-related US stocks and ETFs with NVIDIA over the same three windows.
introScope: Eight categories: AI applications, Agent Infra, consumer electronics, Neocloud, compute, optical interconnects, memory & storage, and grid & modular power.
introFoot: Dates are shared across securities, not chosen to favor each stock. July 29 was identified in hindsight as NVDA's lowest July closing price.
shortCutoff: Fixed snapshot | Oct 30, 2026, around 14:50 ET; market still open
overviewIntro: A security can belong to multiple categories. Category counts overlap; the full universe is deduplicated. Select a phase to rebase prices at that phase's start.

compareIntro: NVDA remains the common benchmark. The table shows returns in each phase and the difference versus NVDA.
analysisTitle: What does the comparison tell us?
analysisIntro: Resilience, rebound size, and loss recovery are three different questions.
methodShort: 77 securities use Futu OpenD forward-adjusted prices; KXIAY uses Yahoo Finance adjusted prices, including split adjustments. Daily closes end on October 29, 2026. The endpoint uses the latest quotes collected around 14:50 ET on October 30; trade times range from 14:02 to 14:50, with KXIAY's delayed quote at 14:35. Returns exclude fees and taxes and are not exact dividend-reinvestment total returns. Volatility is the daily return standard deviation from July 1 to October 29, multiplied by the square root of 252. Maximum drawdowns use complete closing prices only.
methodLimits: This is one drawdown-rebound-drawdown sample with boundaries selected in hindsight. AI relevance does not mean all revenue comes from AI. Historical performance alone does not establish undervaluation or future returns.
